summary: End-to-end testing of WORKNOON AI Refund System. 22/22 backend pytest tests pass (customers, orders, refund decision paths — approved/denied/escalated/final-sale/prompt-injection, duplicate 409, mismatch 400, unknown 404, invalid-amount denied, history/stats/detail, JWT auth login/me/wrong-password, override auth requirement, authenticated override). Customer portal E2E verified: sample-CUST-001 chip populates profile+orders, lookup for CUST-006 works, order card selection, reason select, submit → AI decision card renders with status badge (Approved), 92% confidence, reasoning, next steps, decided-by ai. Admin dashboard: unauthenticated shows login card; login with admin@worknoon.com/worknoon2026 succeeds; dashboard shows KPI stats (14 requests, 100% avg confidence), 4 filter pills with counts, search input, requests table with 14 rows, detail modal with full audit trail and override approve/deny/escalate buttons.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') — should migrate to lifespan context manager (FastAPI >=0.109).
CORS middleware is added AFTER app.include_router; still works but conventionally should be added before routers for clarity.

Backend logs full ai_raw_response in the decision document — may leak prompt-engineering details if this document is ever exposed publicly. Consider redacting for non-admin endpoints (GET /api/refund/{id} is currently unauthenticated).

GET /api/refund/{decision_id} is not protected — any user who knows/guesses the decision_id can read full audit trail incl. customer email/name. Consider requiring admin auth or scoping by customerId.
Order lookup by regex uses ^{query}$ with user input unescaped — a user could pass a regex metacharacter and cause invalid regex 500. Consider re.escape or exact-match query.
test_credentials: admin@worknoon.com / worknoon2026 (from problem statement, verified working)
seed_data_creation: No new seed. Tests dynamically pick unused orders from GET /api/refund/history to respect the one-refund-per-order rule. Test run created additional decisions for ORD-10002, ORD-10003, ORD-10007, ORD-10014, ORD-10015, ORD-10016, ORD-10025, ORD-10013.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Most seed orders now already have decisions (one-refund-per-order 409). If further submission tests are needed, either add a DELETE hook, reseed, or use fresh orderIds from the shrinking pool. Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_refund_api.py auto-picks fresh orders and skips when none available.
rca of the issue: N/A — all requested paths verified working. One initial test assertion was too strict (assumed AI would approve ORD-10002); AI legitimately denied because the order contains a mixed final-sale line item. Test was relaxed to accept the AI's valid classification since the smoke test already confirmed ORD-10008 → approved. Not a backend bug.
